Question: How do I share a folder so that only specific invited users can edit it, and commenters cannot?

**

Hi [Customer Name],

You can share a folder so that only the people you invite can edit it, while anyone you give *Comment* access will be unable to make changes. Follow these steps:

1. **Open the folder you want to share**  
   - In the web app, navigate to the folder and click the **⋮ More options** button (or right‑click the folder).

2. **Select “Share”**  
   - A sharing dialog will appear.

3. **Invite the users who need edit rights**  
   - In the **Invite people** field, type the email addresses of the collaborators.  
   - Click the permission dropdown next to each address and choose **Can edit**.  
   - (Optional) Add a short note if you’d like, then click **Send**.

4. **Add commenters (if you have any)**  
   - If you also want people who can only comment, repeat the invite step for those users but select **Can comment** from the dropdown instead of **Can edit**.  
   - Users with *Can comment* can add comments but cannot modify files or folder structure.

5. **Restrict link‑based access**  
   - At the bottom of the sharing dialog you’ll see **Link sharing**.  
   - Set it to **Only people added can access** (or **Off**). This prevents anyone with the link from gaining edit or comment rights unless you explicitly invite them.

6. **Confirm the permissions**  
   - After you’ve added everyone, you’ll see a list of members with their roles (Edit / Comment).  
   - Verify that only the intended users have the **Can edit** role.

7. **Save / Close**  
   - Click **Done** (or close the dialog). The folder is now shared exactly as you specified.

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Action |
|---|---|
| ✅ | Invite specific users and set their role to **Can edit** |
| ✅ | Invite any commenters and set their role to **Can comment** |
| ✅ | Turn off “Anyone with the link” or set it to **Only people added** |
| ✅ | Double‑check the members list before closing the dialog |

### What happens next?

- **Editors** can add, delete, rename, and move files inside the folder.  
- **Commenters** can view files and leave comments, but they cannot change the folder’s contents.  
- Anyone not on the list will have **no access** at all.

If you run into any trouble (e.g., a user still sees edit options when they should only comment), let me know the email address of the affected user and I can verify the permission settings on our side.

Hope this helps! Let me know if you need anything else.  

Best regards,  
[Your Name]  
Customer Support – [Your Company]

**

Hi [Customer Name],

You can share a folder so that only the people you invite can edit it, while anyone you give *comment* access will not be able to make changes. Follow the steps below:

---

### 1. Open the folder you want to share
1. In the left‑hand navigation, locate the folder.
2. Click the **⋮ More options** button next to the folder name (or right‑click the folder) and choose **Share**.

### 2. Invite the users who need edit rights
1. In the **Invite people** field, type the email addresses of the collaborators who should be able to edit.
2. Click the **Permission** dropdown next to the field and select **Can edit**.
3. (Optional) Add a personal note, then click **Send invitation**.

> **Result:** Those users will receive an email invitation and will have full edit rights inside the folder and all its contents.

### 3. Add commenters (people who should only comment)
1. In the same **Share** dialog, click **Add people** again.
2. Enter the email addresses of the people who should only comment.
3. From the **Permission** dropdown, choose **Can comment**.
4. Click **Send invitation**.

> **Result:** Commenters can open files, add comments, and view the folder, but they cannot modify or delete any files.

### 4. Restrict link‑based access (so only invited users can act)
1. Still in the **Share** dialog, look at the **Link sharing** section at the bottom.
2. Set **Link access** to **Only people added can open** (or **Off** if you don’t want a shareable link at all).
3. Click **Save**.

> This ensures that anyone who isn’t explicitly invited (even if they have the link) cannot view or edit the folder.

### 5. Verify the permissions
1. After you’ve sent the invitations, return to the folder and open **Share** again.
2. You’ll see a list of members with their assigned roles (Can edit / Can comment).  
   - **Can edit** → full edit rights.  
   - **Can comment** → view + comment only.  

If you need to change a user’s role later, simply click the role next to their name and select a different permission.

---

## Quick checklist

| Step | Action | Result |
|------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Open **Share** for the folder | Dialog appears |
| 2 | Invite editors → **Can edit** | Editors can modify files |
| 3 | Invite commenters → **Can comment** | Commenters can only comment |
| 4 | Set **Link access** to “Only people added” | No one else can get in |
| 5 | Review the members list | Confirm correct roles |

---

### Common pitfalls & how to avoid them
| Issue | Why it happens | Fix |
|-------|----------------|-----|
| Commenters can still edit | They were given **Can edit** by mistake or the folder inherited edit rights from a parent folder. | Re‑open **Share**, change their role to **Can comment**, and ensure the parent folder isn’t set to “Anyone with the link can edit”. |
| Uninvited users can view the folder | Link sharing is set to “Anyone with the link can view”. | Switch link sharing to “Only people added can open”. |
| New files inherit wrong permissions | Files created by an editor inherit that editor’s default permissions. | After creating a file, double‑check its sharing settings or set the folder’s default permission to “Can comment” for new members, then manually upgrade the needed editors. |

---

### Need more help?
If you run into any trouble (e.g., a user isn’t receiving the invitation, or you see an unexpected permission level), just let me know their email address and I can check the account status or any sync limits that might be affecting sharing.

Thanks for reaching out, and happy collaborating!
